result.instructions: RightClick X is a live, self-composing capability graph. Start with context_research (optionally with a topic) to see what this environment can do, context_learn to add any URL, context_compose to turn what you have into what you want across providers, and context_run to execute. The tool list never changes; the graph behind it does.

tools.name: context_runtime
tools.description: Identify this RightClick X instance: version, runtime (node/bun/deno/workers/browser), region, graph size and powers, receipt-chain head.
tools.title: Identify this RightClick X instance

tools.name: context_research
tools.description: Research the environment: what runtime and platform bindings exist, which semantic types the graph produces and consumes, which inputs have no producer yet (gaps), and — given a topic — which public sources worldwide (APIs.guru OpenAPI directory, the official MCP Registry) could add powers. Pass learn:N to pull the top N candidates straight into the graph.

learn.description: Learn the top N candidates immediately.

tools.title: Survey the environment and directories

tools.name: context_learn
tools.description: Point RightClick X at any URL. It detects what is there (OpenAPI/Swagger spec, GraphQL endpoint, MCP server, another RightClick X peer, or a web page whose forms become capabilities), reflects it into typed capabilities, and reports how many new capabilities and composite powers the graph gained.

source.description: URL of a spec, endpoint, server, peer or page.

deep.description: Also probe well-known locations at the origin.

tools.title: Learn a source's capabilities

tools.name: context_forget
tools.description: Remove a provider and its capabilities from the live graph.
tools.title: Forget a provider

tools.name: context_inspect
tools.description: Classify any value into the semantic type lattice (url, email, language, place, geo.lat, html, markdown, json, ...).
tools.title: Classify a value

tools.name: context_actions
tools.description: What can be done with this value right now: capabilities that accept it directly, plus every semantic type it can be turned into through multi-step pipelines.

type.description: Or a semantic type instead of a value.

tools.title: What can be done with a value

annotations.title: What can be done with a value

tools.name: context_explain
tools.description: Everything about one capability: typed ports, provider, risk label, how it is invoked, its neighbours in the graph, observed reliability and latency, and example arguments.
tools.title: Explain a capability

tools.name: context_run
tools.description: Run one capability now. Saved goal:<slug> capabilities re-plan against the current environment, heal API changes and repeat their stored result checks and independent witnesses. Returns output, timing, receipt, verification and witness evidence. Optional predicates add checks; they never remove stored checks.

verify.description: Outcome checks on the result, e.g. [{"op":"contains","value":"Lisbon"}, {"op":"gt","path":"temperature","value":-50}]. ops: exists, equals, contains, matches, type, gt, lt, length_gt.

tools.title: Run a capability

tools.name: context_run_status
tools.description: Read a previous run by runId, or list recent runs. Also reports whether the receipt chain is intact.
tools.title: Read run receipts

tools.name: context_compose
tools.description: Give what you have and the type you want; RightClick X discovers routes across the environment and (with run:true) executes, checks and repairs them. Currency/unit refinements require explicit conversions. Attach witnesses for independent business-outcome checks. publish saves a stable goal:<slug> capability another AI can discover with context_graph and invoke with context_run; its checks survive restart and API changes. A successful multi-step pipeline is also saved for reuse.

want.description: Desired semantic type, e.g. text, language, geo.lat, html, hash.

intent.description: Words describing the goal, e.g. 'weather forecast translated'.

verify.description: Outcome checks on the result, e.g. [{"op":"contains","value":"Lisbon"}, {"op":"gt","path":"temperature","value":-50}]. ops: exists, equals, contains, matches, type, gt, lt, length_gt.

witnesses.description: Independent outcome checks, repeated for every saved invocation. Discover a read-only checker in the environment. Example: [{"capability":"<checker id>","args":{"order_id":{"input":"order_id"},"tax_amount":{"output":""}},"verify":[{"op":"equals","path":"valid","value":true}]}]. input paths read this invocation's have values; output paths read the candidate result (empty string = whole result); value supplies a literal. The checker must be a separate provider and must pass its predicates. Its contract is pinned on save; a changed checker fails closed.

output.description: Path in the candidate output; empty string selects all of it.

verify.description: Outcome checks on the result, e.g. [{"op":"contains","value":"Lisbon"}, {"op":"gt","path":"temperature","value":-50}]. ops: exists, equals, contains, matches, type, gt, lt, length_gt.

confirm.description: Required to run plans containing destructive capabilities.

publish.description: After a successful run, save this goal as goal:<slug> in the graph AND as /x/<slug> in the synthesized API. Checks and witnesses are retained and re-run on every invocation. Supply checks/witnesses to establish verified outcomes.

acquire.description: If nothing in the graph can do it: research public directories (APIs.guru, MCP Registry), learn the best candidates and re-plan.

through.description: Anchors: capability ids or search phrases the pipeline must pass through; the planner wires the types between them.

risks.description: Optional constraint: plan only with these risk labels, e.g. ["read"].

tools.title: Compose and run a workflow

tools.name: context_graph
tools.description: Query the live graph. op: stats | types | search (query) | neighbors (id) | paths (from, to) | edges | export.
tools.title: Query the capability graph

tools.name: context_providers
tools.description: Providers currently contributing capabilities: builtins, platform, OpenAPI, GraphQL, MCP, web, peers, crystallized pipelines.
tools.title: List providers

tools.name: context_watch
tools.description: Follow the graph as it changes: providers learned/forgotten, runs, crystallizations, research. Pass the returned cursor back as since; waitMs long-polls.

waitMs.description: Wait up to this long for new events.

tools.title: Follow graph changes
